**PocketPulse**  
*Your money. Your rules. Your pace.*  
     
   [![](data:image/png;base64,)  
   ![](data:image/png;base64,)  
   ![](data:image/png;base64,)  
 ](LICENSE "LICENSE")  
   A command-line expense tracker for students. Type what you spent the way you'd say it, and PocketPulse works out the amount, the currency and the category, then shows where your money goes. Everything stays on your computer: no accounts, no cloud, no network access.  
   
   [Install · ](#anchor-1 "#anchor-1")[Screenshots · ](#anchor-2 "#anchor-2")[Usage · ](#anchor-3 "#anchor-3")[Features · ](#anchor-4 "#anchor-4")[Changelog  
 ](CHANGELOG.md "CHANGELOG.md")  
     
   
**Features**  
- **Natural entry.**chips 20, spent 40 on samosa, coffee $5, 50/- petrol. Ambiguous input (two numbers, no amount) is asked about, never guessed.  
- **Smart categories, offline.** A deterministic keyword matcher suggests a category and tells you why. Change one and PocketPulse offers to remember it. Add your own categories and keywords.  
- **Multi-currency.** INR by default, plus USD, EUR, GBP, AED, CAD, AUD, JPY and SGD. Each expense keeps its own currency and different currencies are never added together.  
- **Dashboard and analytics.** Today, this week, this month, category breakdowns, daily charts, previous periods, custom date ranges and spending trends. Comparisons are fair: a half-finished week is compared with the same days of last week.  
- **Interactive menu** with arrow keys and one-key shortcuts, or plain commands for scripting.  
- **Local and private.** One SQLite file in your user data folder. An automated test fails if any source file imports a networking module.  
- **Looks right everywhere.** Seven colour themes, truecolor down to no colour (NO_COLOR is respected), an ASCII fallback, and layouts that adapt to the window size.  
**A quick look**  
Screenshots use sample data and are rendered from the program's real output.  
**Add an expense in plain language.** PocketPulse shows what it understood, suggests a category and says why, and asks before saving.  
**The home screen.** Arrow keys or one-letter shortcuts, with the dashboard above the menu.  
**Weekly and monthly analytics.** Totals, averages, the busiest day, bar charts and a comparison with the previous period.  
**Themes.** Seven of them, with ocean as the default.  
**Install**  
Requires **Node.js 22.13 or newer**. There are no npm dependencies.  
git clone https://github.com/prince2bit/pocketpulse.git  
 cd pocketpulse  
 node src/index.js            # run it  
 npm link                     # optional: puts the `pocketpulse` command on your PATH  
   
**Usage**  
pocketpulse                          # dashboard and menu (first run asks for your main currency)  
 pocketpulse add chips 20             # quick add, with a preview and confirmation  
 pocketpulse add "protein bar" 120 --category Fitness  
 pocketpulse list                     # recent expenses  
 pocketpulse today                    # everything spent today  
 pocketpulse week --previous          # last week (also: month, range, trends)  
 pocketpulse month 2026-10  
 pocketpulse range 2026-11-01 2026-11-20  
 pocketpulse trends --weeks 12  
 pocketpulse week --category "Food & Snacks"  
   
 pocketpulse categories add "Fitness" --icon 🏋️ --color orange  
 pocketpulse categories teach "protein bar" Fitness  
 pocketpulse settings currency USD  
 pocketpulse themes  
 pocketpulse --help  
   
**How categorisation works**  
1. The description is split into lowercase words, with plurals reduced (chips matches chip).  
2. Every keyword rule whose words appear together, in order, is a candidate.  
3. Your own rules beat the built-in ones, and a longer phrase beats a word inside it (water bottle is Shopping, water is Food & Drinks).  
4. If words point to different categories (chips and chai), the best match is suggested and the alternatives are shown.  
5. No match means **Other**.  
There is no AI and no network involved, and the same input always gives the same answer. The vocabulary is English with some Indian terms; teach PocketPulse your own with categories teach.  
**Your data**  
Everything lives in one SQLite file:  
| | |  
|-|-|  
| **System** | **Location** |   
| Linux | ~/.local/share/pocketpulse/pocketpulse.db |   
| macOS | ~/Library/Application Support/PocketPulse/pocketpulse.db |   
| Windows | %APPDATA%\PocketPulse\pocketpulse.db |   
   
Set POCKETPULSE_HOME to use a different folder. The file is outside this repository, and .gitignore blocks database files.  
**Current limitations**  
This is an early version.  
- **You can't edit or delete an expense yet.** A wrong entry can only be avoided at the confirmation step. Editing, deleting and undo are the next thing on the list.  
- No export or backup command yet (the database is a single file you can copy).  
- No budgets yet.  
- Developed and tested on Linux with Node 22. Windows and macOS should work, and the included CI workflow is set up to run the tests on both, but they have had less real-world use.  
**Roadmap**  
- **0.2:** edit and delete expenses with undo, recategorise old expenses, search and filters in list.  
- **0.3:** optional budgets with gentle warnings, CSV and JSON export, backup and restore.  
**Development**  
npm test                 # unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Node's built-in runner)  
 npm run release:check    # fails while placeholder text is left in the repository  
   
src/  
   index.js        entry point  
   app.js          wires database, repositories and services together  
   cli/            commands, router, interactive home screen  
   services/       business rules (expenses, categories, parsing, analytics)  
   database/       connection, migrations, SQL repositories, seed data  
   ui/             theme, panels, charts, dashboard and report rendering, prompts  
   utils/          money, dates, text helpers  
 tests/            mirrors the above, plus end-to-end tests that run the real program  
   
The screenshots in docs/images are generated from the real code with a fixed sample dataset: node scripts/screenshots.mjs writes SVGs, and python3 scripts/svg-to-png.py (needs Playwright) rasterises them.
